subject: science
passage: Great tits living in noisy parts of cities tend to sing songs with higher minimum pitches than great tits in quieter areas. A widely cited explanation is that traffic noise is concentrated at low frequencies, so birds that shift their songs upward are more easily heard by rivals and potential mates. <u>Some researchers, however, point out that when birds sing more loudly, their songs often rise in pitch as a side effect, much as human voices do when people shout.</u> If that is the case, higher urban songs may reflect birds simply singing louder over the din rather than adjusting their pitch to escape it, and experiments are now trying to separate the two possibilities.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It shows that the widely cited explanation has already been disproved by controlled experiments.
choices.B: It introduces an alternative account of the pattern described at the beginning of the text.
choices.C: It explains why birds with higher-pitched songs are more easily heard by their rivals and mates.
choices.D: It provides evidence that traffic noise in cities is concentrated mainly at low frequencies.

explanation.why: The first two sentences describe a pattern (higher songs in noisy areas) and the usual explanation (birds move above low-frequency noise). The underlined sentence, introduced by "however," raises another possibility: the higher pitch may be a side effect of singing louder. The last sentence calls these "the two possibilities."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says experiments "are now trying to separate the two possibilities," so neither has been disproved.
explanation.B: Correct. It suggests higher pitch may be a by-product of louder singing, which the final sentence treats as one of "two possibilities."
explanation.C: Incorrect. That is the reasoning of the first explanation; the underlined sentence offers a different one.
explanation.D: Incorrect. That claim belongs to the widely cited explanation in the second sentence; the underlined sentence is about loudness and pitch.
